country_overview: South Africa operates a floating exchange rate regime administered by the South African Reserve Bank (SARB). The Rand is subject to certain capital flow management measures and reporting requirements, while current account transactions are largely liberalised.

summary.traveler: Travelers may bring in foreign currency without limit but must declare amounts of ZAR 25,000 or equivalent. Export of foreign currency is restricted and subject to SARB rules.
summary.business: Businesses must route significant foreign exchange transactions through authorised banks. Capital repatriation and certain payments require SARB approval or documentation.

rules.bring_foreign_currency_in: Foreign currency may be brought into South Africa without limit. Amounts of ZAR 25,000 or equivalent must be declared to South African Revenue Service (SARS) upon arrival.
rules.take_foreign_currency_out: Foreign currency may be taken out up to the amount declared on entry or supported by authorised bank documentation. Residents are subject to SARB limits.
rules.cash_declaration_threshold: ZAR 25,000 or equivalent in foreign currency or negotiable instruments at entry and exit. Declaration to SARS is mandatory.
rules.resident_holding_rules: South African residents are subject to SARB limits and approval requirements when holding or using foreign currency accounts. General unrestricted access requires specific authorisation.
rules.non_resident_rules: Non-residents may open and operate foreign currency accounts and transfer funds more freely through authorised banks.
rules.business_invoicing_settlement: Cross-border business transactions must be settled through authorised banks in accordance with SARB foreign exchange regulations.
rules.exchange_controls: South Africa maintains a floating exchange regime with controls on certain capital account transactions. Current account transactions are largely liberalised.
rules.banking_conversion_practicality: Foreign exchange conversion is available through authorised banks and licensed exchange offices. Documentation is required for large transactions.
